title: Backtracking

views.title: Backtracking
views.intro: Choose, explore, undo. Subsets and combinations move a START index forward; permutations use a used[] array. For duplicate inputs sort first and skip equal siblings at the same depth. Prune early with a cheap feasibility bound.
table: used[] array, with duplicate skip rule
N-Queens, sudoku with occupancy sets or bitmasks

files.desc: Subsets (+dup), permutations (+unique), combinations, combination sum I/II, parentheses, phone, palindrome partition, word search, N-Queens, sudoku, IP addresses, add operators, gray code

pitfalls: Add a COPY of the current path to the result, not the live list.
Duplicates: `i > start && a[i] == a[i-1]` for combinations; `used[i-1]` check for permutations.
Prune before recursing (remaining sum < 0, not enough elements left) instead of after.

views.title: Backtracking: Pruning & Structure
views.intro: Hard backtracking is about cutting the tree: sort and skip symmetric branches, count by symmetry, use BFS when the question is "minimum steps", or skip the search entirely when a formula (factorial number system) picks the answer.
table: Net balances, backtrack on first non-zero

files.desc: Matchsticks to square, unique paths III, combination sum III, permutation sequence, palindrome permutations, letter case permutation, different ways to add parentheses, remove invalid parentheses, max length of unique-char concatenation, Android unlock patterns, generalized abbreviation, optimal account balancing, all paths in a DAG

pitfalls: Equal-state siblings explore the same subtree: skip a bucket with the same load as an earlier one.
Undo exactly what you did (restore cells, pop path entries, reset lengths).
If the question asks for the k-th item, do not enumerate.
